deviation: Availability is 99.5% (the playbook fallback, not the 99.9% standard), and the draft drops service credits entirely, leaving only investigation, remediation and a root-cause report on request. The draft also adds exclusions for scheduled maintenance and events beyond Supplier's reasonable control, and a 48-hour security incident notice that is looser than a typical data protection standard. Without credits Arcadia has no financial remedy for downtime, and it must prove repeated failure to get a material breach.
suggested_text: The Supplier shall achieve at least 99.9% availability each month and shall issue service credits of 5% of monthly fees for each full 1% shortfall. Availability excludes only scheduled maintenance notified to Customer in advance in accordance with the agreed maintenance window, and outages caused by Customer. Supplier shall promptly investigate and remedy any failure to meet the availability commitment and provide Customer a written root-cause report on request. Service credits are without prejudice to Customer's other rights and remedies, including under clause 14 for repeated failure. Supplier shall notify Customer of any security incident affecting the Services or Customer Data without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, and shall provide all information and cooperation Customer reasonably requires.
